00-holdup.text: A blind user holds up a medicine box. HoldUp runs on the Gemini Live API: camera and voice in, speech out. It reads the strength aloud and says when it is not sure. Zero of seven hundred fifty-four confident strength reads were wrong.

01-hook.text: How do you earn that trust in an agent? Canary Lab: Gemini plays, attacks and explains an insider-threat benchmark.

03-ladder.text: So Gemini plays. Five models, up to four thinking levels, five hundred eighty-seven paired episodes. On hard, Gemini four Carbon on high thinking reaches one hundred six percent of the solver, interval ninety-four to one hundred twenty-six, at one dollar ninety-three per episode. Gemini three point six Flash on high thinking costs forty-five cents, more than four times cheaper, and scores eighty-eight percent, interval fifty-one to one hundred thirty-eight: not distinguishable from the solver, but less certain.

04-atlas.text: Then Gemini reads. All 153 trajectories in one cached context, without our labels. Blind, it recovered 3 of 5 failure modes our code defines and named 2 new ones. Coverage is still weak: the steps it cites hold 21 percent of all regret.

05-swarm.text: Then Gemini attacks. One hundred attacks in four waves, most with our whole codebase in context. Zero verified exploits. To test the detector, we reopened a closed hole: it caught four of four.

06-innovative.text: That is the innovation: a benchmark that measures, explains and audits itself. Across two hundred ninety-five episodes, every lost point is tagged to a decision, with nothing unexplained.

07-essential.text: Three Gemini features make this possible. Thinking level is the ladder's knob. Thought signatures keep reasoning across tool calls. The explicit cache served most input tokens, and every Gemini call is logged. TTS and Live only narrate.

08-close.text: Recorded Gemini runs replay offline. Make lab replay. No key needed.
